lines.name: Santa Fe trains, Stockton to Richmond and Ferry Point

operators.name: Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway

lines.summary: The Santa Fe's trains from Chicago and the San Joaquin Valley, from Stockton across the Delta and along Suisun Bay and San Pablo Bay to Richmond, and until 1933 through the tunnel to its ferry at Ferry Point, Point Richmond.
lines.fate_note: From April 23, 1933 the trains ended at Richmond and ran on to Oakland (Time Table No. 68); the line still carries BNSF's freight and, east of Bay Point, the Gold Runner.

route.note: To August 18, 1918, when under federal control the trains went to the Southern Pacific's Oakland Pier instead.
Back from January 9, 1921 (Time Table No. 47) until April 23, 1933 (No. 68).

running.note: Nos. 1 and 2 at Richmond; No. 17 of May 30, 1971 schedules no passenger train.

sources.note: "The first through train from Chicago, over the Santa Fe, arrived on July 3, 1900, about noon", with the ferry Ocean Wave waiting.
"Stockton to Point Richmond, 70.39 miles, May 1, 1900", put in operation.
Freight "by May 1"; "Through passengers will probably not be taken until two months later."
"The operation of the property was formally taken over by Santa Fe officials on July 17, 1900".

lines.notes: Opens with the first through train from Chicago, July 3, 1900 (the county history of 1926, written by a resident of the time); the line had been put in operation for freight on May 1, and the Santa Fe formally took it over on July 17. The San Francisco Call of July 2, 1900 has the story (page 3), still to be read. Under federal control, from August 18, 1918 the trains ran from Richmond to the Southern Pacific's Oakland Pier instead (CRC Decision No. 5642; Time Table No. 44), until the Santa Fe's own ferry came back, on January 9, 1921 by Time Table No. 47, whose cover shows the date put off twice. When its last passenger train ran at Richmond isn't sourced: the timetables show trains in June 1968 and none in May 1971, so it is drawn to 1968. Its trains to Oakland (from 1904 or so) aren't drawn yet.

lines.name: Santa Fe ferry, Ferry Point to San Francisco

operators.name: Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway

lines.summary: The Santa Fe's own boats from its train shed at Ferry Point, Point Richmond, to the foot of Market St, meeting every train.
lines.fate_note: Given up when the Interstate Commerce Commission let the Santa Fe and the Western Pacific use the Southern Pacific's ferries instead; from April 23, 1933 the trains ran to Oakland Pier.

sources.note: The ferry Ocean Wave met the first through train, July 3, 1900.
To be "abandoned … in the latter part of April".

lines.notes: Ends on April 23, 1933, the day Time Table No. 68 dropped Ferry Point; the last run itself isn't dated, and the Commission's order isn't found. Under federal control, from August 18, 1918 the trains ran from Richmond to the Southern Pacific's Oakland Pier instead (CRC Decision No. 5642; Time Table No. 44), until the Santa Fe's own ferry came back, on January 9, 1921 by Time Table No. 47, whose cover shows the date put off twice. Which slip at the Ferry Building it used isn't sourced.
